q: בת 84, ברקע יתר לחץ דם, עודף משקל, היפרתירואידיזם, מעשנת כבדה. במעקב שגרתי במרפאה נצפו דפורמציות באצבעות כפות הידיים. מה מגורמי הרקע שלה הוא גורם סיכון לממצאים שנראו בידיים?
o: עודף משקל
יתר לחץ דם
היפרתירואידיזם
עישון
explanation:
Bony enlargement at distal or proximal interphalangeal joints and involvement of the thumb base suggest hand osteoarthritis. Finger deformity alone cannot confirm its cause. **If the enlarged interphalangeal joints represent nodal hand osteoarthritis, overweight is the relevant risk factor** among this woman's conditions.

**A. Overweight.** The association extends to the non-weight-bearing hand. Body weight can therefore be relevant even when mechanical loading is not the full explanation.
**B. Hypertension.** Its weak relationship with hand osteoarthritis in the Rotterdam cohort disappeared after adjustment for BMI.
**C. Hyperthyroidism.** Thyroid excess can reduce bone mass, but it is not the characteristic association with nodal interphalangeal osteoarthritis.
**D. Smoking.** Smoking history is relevant when considering other rheumatic illnesses, but cannot identify the cause of these deformities. Examine the joint distribution and look for active synovitis.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 780–782. Dahaghin et al., Ann Rheum Dis, 2007, doi:10.1136/ard.2005.045724.

q: גבר בן 78 שנים עם היסטוריה של סוכרת הופקד לאשפוז עם דלקת ריאות. בחקירה קלינית: דופק 105/דקה, לחץ דם 92/58, טמפרטורה 38.5°C. למרות טיפול אנטיביוטי מתאים, המטופל אינו מגיב כצפוי ותמותתו עולה משמעותית. איזה מהגורמים הביולוגיים הבאים מסביר בעיקר את תגובת החיסון המוגבלת בקשישים?
o: ירידה בתפקוד תאי T ובוגרות תאי B
עלייה בסינתזת אנטיגנים
הגברת הפקת ציטוקינים פרו-דלקתיים
ירידה בשיעור ההתחלקות של תאים דם לבנים
explanation:
Aging can weaken adaptive responses to unfamiliar antigens even when baseline inflammation is high. **Reduced T-cell responsiveness and impaired B-cell antibody maturation** help explain vulnerability to infection. The clinical course of pneumonia alone cannot isolate one immune defect.

**A. T-cell function and B-cell maturation.** A narrower naïve T-cell repertoire and impaired antibody class switching or maturation can weaken an antigen-specific response.
**B. Increased antigen synthesis.** Antigens are targets of recognition. Their production does not explain the patient's impaired capacity to mount an adaptive response.
**C. Increased proinflammatory cytokines.** Chronic low-grade inflammation may coexist with a weaker response to a new infection and does not supply the full adaptive mechanism.
**D. Reduced white-cell division.** Antigen-stimulated proliferation of some T cells can decline with age. “White-cell division” leaves the cell type and stimulus unspecified, and changes in memory-cell numbers do not measure their present division rate.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 47, 56. Human T-cell proliferative response and aging, PMID 3127423.
ref: Hazzard Ch 1 — BIOLOGY OF AGING AND LONGEVITY

q: A 79-year-old woman with sarcopenia is receiving nutritional advice and asks what to add to improve muscle strength and function. Which intervention is the evidence-supported cornerstone described by Hazzard?
o: A regular aerobic walking program as the main exercise component
A regular resistance exercise program started with expert professional supervision
Vitamin D supplementation for muscle function without severe vitamin deficiency
Growth hormone treatment to increase the amount of skeletal muscle
explanation:
Sarcopenia impairs muscle strength and function. **Add progressive resistance exercise, initially supervised**, to nutrition therapy so muscle groups practice generating force against a load.

**A. Aerobic walking.** Walking can improve endurance but does not replace a structured strengthening program.
**B. Supervised resistance exercise.** A professional can choose safe loads and progress exercises for the upper and lower limbs.
**C. Vitamin D without severe deficiency.** Correction of deficiency may be appropriate. Supplementation alone is not the established strengthening treatment here.
**D. Growth hormone.** An increase in lean mass does not guarantee improved strength or function and does not justify routine hormone treatment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 737.
ref: Hazzard Ch 49 — MUSCLE AGING AND SARCOPENIA

q: חולה עם דמנציה הוגדרה בישראל כחולה הנוטה למות שאינה בעלת כשרות. לפני הכרעה לגבי רצונה בהארכת חיים, איזה מידע יש לברר לפי סעיף 5(ב)?
o: את רצון הבת שהביעה העדפה לטיפול המרחיב ביותר
את רצון הבן שהביע העדפה לטיפול המצמצם ביותר
הנחיות תקפות, החלטת מיופה כוח או החלטת ועדה
את העדפת הצוות במשמרת שהכיר אותה לאחרונה
explanation:
בבירור רצונו של אדם חסר כשרות בודקים תחילה את מקורות ההכרעה שהחוק מכיר בהם. **הנחיות תקפות, החלטת מיופה כוח או החלטת ועדה**.

**א. את רצון הבת שהביעה העדפה לטיפול המרחיב ביותר.** הבת יכולה למסור מידע על רצונו, לא לבחור את היקף הטיפול לפי טעמה.
**ב. את רצון הבן שהביע העדפה לטיפול המצמצם ביותר.** אותו כלל חל גם אם הבן מעוניין בצמצום הטיפול.
**ג. הנחיות תקפות, החלטת מיופה כוח או החלטת ועדה.** הנחיות מקדימות, מינוי תקף והכרעת ועדה עשויים לקבוע את הרצון לפי העניין.
**ד. את העדפת הצוות במשמרת שהכיר אותה לאחרונה.** העדפת הצוות אינה תחליף למקורות האלה.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, תשס״ו-2005, עמ׳ 5.

q: An 84-year-old woman with frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 6), COPD requiring home oxygen, and stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 22) lives alone, uses a walker, and receives help from her daughter with shopping and medication. She takes furosemide 40 mg twice daily, spironolactone 25 mg daily, and albuterol as needed. Potassium is 5.8, creatinine 2.8 (stable), and bicarbonate 18. She feels well apart from mild fatigue. Which change addresses Hazzard's contraindication to continuing mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist treatment?
o: Stop spironolactone given hyperkalemia and renal dysfunction.
Continue spironolactone while adding oral sodium bicarbonate.
Continue spironolactone while reducing the dose of furosemide.
Continue spironolactone while adding a potassium-binding agent.
explanation:
Spironolactone can worsen hyperkalemia when renal function is severely reduced. **Stop spironolactone and promptly assess and manage the potassium of 5.8** in this patient with eGFR 22.

**A. Stop the MRA.** This removes a potassium-retaining drug in a high-risk clinical setting.
**B. Continue with bicarbonate.** Treating acidosis does not remove the contraindicated exposure.
**C. Reduce furosemide.** Less loop diuretic may reduce potassium excretion and still leaves spironolactone.
**D. Continue with a binder.** A binder may treat potassium in selected settings but does not itself resolve the stated reason to stop the MRA.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1181.

q: An 88-year-old man with mild dementia, BPH, osteoarthritis, and insomnia has become increasingly confused over three days and no longer recognizes family. One week ago he started diphenhydramine 50 mg at bedtime and oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily. Vital signs are stable and CAM screening is positive. Which medication plan applies Beers 2023 guidance to minimize his anticholinergic burden?
o: Discontinue both diphenhydramine and oxybutynin, then reassess symptoms.
Replace diphenhydramine with oral doxylamine and continue oxybutynin.
Replace oxybutynin with oral tolterodine and continue diphenhydramine.
Continue both diphenhydramine and oxybutynin while monitoring symptoms.
explanation:
Starting two strong anticholinergics together can increase confusion and fall risk. Both new drugs belong in the immediate review of this man’s delirium.

**Stop diphenhydramine and oxybutynin and reassess.** Removing both exposures gives his cognition a chance to improve while other causes are investigated.

**A. Stop both.** This removes the new antihistamine and bladder antimuscarinic that together increased his burden.
**B. Use doxylamine and retain oxybutynin.** Doxylamine is another strongly anticholinergic antihistamine, so the combination persists.
**C. Use tolterodine and retain diphenhydramine.** Tolterodine is also a bladder antimuscarinic, so two anticholinergic drugs remain.
**D. Monitor both.** Observation while continuing both drugs leaves the potentially reversible burden unchanged.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2066, 2070, 2074.

q: A 75-year-old woman with recently diagnosed mild cognitive impairment developed worsening confusion after starting solifenacin for urgency urinary incontinence. Her clinician plans to replace the antimuscarinic with a beta-3 agonist. Which prescription matches that class in Hazzard?
o: Oxybutynin for urgency urinary incontinence
Mirabegron for urgency urinary incontinence
Tolterodine for urgency urinary incontinence
Solifenacin for urgency urinary incontinence
explanation:
Solifenacin blocks muscarinic receptors and may worsen cognition in a vulnerable patient. **Mirabegron is a beta-3 agonist** used to relax the bladder during filling.

**A. Oxybutynin for urgency urinary incontinence.** Oxybutynin is another antimuscarinic and can worsen cognitive adverse effects.
**B. Mirabegron for urgency urinary incontinence.** Mirabegron changes drug class. Review blood pressure and emptying when assessing suitability.
**C. Tolterodine for urgency urinary incontinence.** Tolterodine remains an antimuscarinic.
**D. Solifenacin for urgency urinary incontinence.** Continuing solifenacin keeps the exposure under review.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 712, 713.

q: A 77-year-old woman reports dizziness when wearing high-necked sweaters or adjusting necklaces. Yesterday she briefly lost consciousness during hair washing at a salon. She has coronary artery disease treated with stenting and hypertension, and takes aspirin 81 mg daily, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. If contraindications are excluded, which test directly evaluates suspected carotid sinus hypersensitivity?
o: Carotid ultrasound with Doppler blood-flow assessment.
Carotid sinus massage with continuous monitoring.
Twenty-four-hour Holter monitoring with ambulatory ECG recording.
Tilt-table testing with an infusion of isoproterenol.
explanation:
Pressure from a collar or hair washing can trigger an excessive carotid sinus reflex, causing bradycardia or hypotension. **Monitored carotid sinus massage by a trained clinician** tests the reflex after contraindications are excluded.

**A. Carotid Doppler.** It assesses arterial flow and narrowing, not the reflex response to neck pressure.
**B. Monitored carotid sinus massage.** Monitor ECG and blood pressure to correlate a reflex response with symptoms.
**C. Ambulatory Holter.** It can identify spontaneous rhythm disturbances but does not directly assess this trigger.
**D. Tilt-table provocation.** It assesses responses to upright posture, a different stimulus.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 669, 671–672.

q: A 78-year-old woman with moderate dementia (MMSE 18/30) has lost 8 kg in six months and now needs help bathing. She denies complaints. She takes donepezil 10 mg, metformin 500 mg twice daily, and atorvastatin 20 mg. Albumin is 2.8, hemoglobin 10.2, and TSH is normal. Her daughter asks about appetite stimulants. After reversible causes have been addressed, which approach is supported without assuming proven benefit from an appetite stimulant?
o: Use mirtazapine for weight gain without establishing depression.
Use megestrol for expected gains in function and quality of life.
Use dronabinol for established clinical benefits in older adults.
Adjust the meal environment and provide feeding assistance.
explanation:
Dementia can impair attention to food and the ability to initiate or finish a meal. Once reversible causes of weight loss are addressed, **adapt the dining environment and provide feeding assistance**.

**A. Mirtazapine solely for weight.** Evidence for weight benefit in the absence of depression is weak.
**B. Megestrol for function.** Any gain tends to be fat, with no demonstrated functional benefit and meaningful adverse effects.
**C. Dronabinol.** Small studies in older adults do not establish dependable clinical benefit.
**D. Feeding assistance.** Cueing, help with utensils and a suitable environment directly address barriers to eating.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 427–429.

q: A 73-year-old woman with hypertension takes a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug for joint pain. What is the role of reviewing this medication in her blood pressure evaluation?
o: Identifying a medication contributing to elevated blood pressure
Identifying a medication providing an antihypertensive effect
Identifying a medication replacing repeated blood pressure measurements
Identifying a medication making standing blood pressure measurement unnecessary
explanation:
NSAIDs can raise blood pressure through renal sodium retention and can blunt some antihypertensive effects. **Review the NSAID as a potentially reversible contributor to hypertension**.

**A. Contributing medication.** Ask about prescribed and over-the-counter doses and assess safer pain options.
**B. Antihypertensive effect.** NSAIDs are analgesics and may increase pressure.
**C. Replace repeated measurements.** Medication history cannot confirm the level or persistence of hypertension.
**D. Standing measurement unnecessary.** Orthostatic assessment remains relevant in older patients.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1222.

q: An older woman receiving an opioid has constipation. Examination identifies a large, firm rectal impaction, without peritoneal signs or suspected perforation. According to Hazzard, what should precede insertion of an enema or suppository?
o: Administer a soapsuds enema to soften the impacted stool.
Begin docusate and wait for the impacted stool to pass.
Insert a suppository before attempting to remove the impaction.
Manually evacuate the large mass of hard rectal stool.
explanation:
A large firm mass in the rectum prevents easy evacuation. **Manually remove the impacted stool before inserting an enema or suppository**, taking care to minimize pain.

**A. Administer a soapsuds enema to soften the impacted stool.** Soapsuds can irritate the mucosa and are not the first step for an accessible hard impaction.
**B. Begin docusate and wait for the impacted stool to pass.** Docusate is not a reliable method of clearing this obstruction.
**C. Insert a suppository before attempting to remove the impaction.** A suppository alone cannot reliably clear a large, hard plug. Remove the accessible mass first, then reassess remaining stool.
**D. Manually evacuate the large mass of hard rectal stool.** A large, hard mass already in the rectum needs direct clearance. Gentle manual evacuation relieves the obstruction and makes subsequent rectal treatment more effective.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1376.

q: מה מאפיין את השינויים בלבלב בגיל המבוגר ?
o: יש ירידה בתפקוד האקסוקריני של הלבלב
יש עליה בנפח הלבלב משני להסננה שומנית
יש עליה בלחץ של ה- SPHINCTER OF ODI
יש ירידה במשקל הלבלב
explanation:
Aging is associated with **reduced exocrine secretory reserve and loss of pancreatic parenchymal mass**. Fatty replacement can coexist with a smaller or lighter gland.

**A. Reduced exocrine function.** Enzyme or bicarbonate output can decline, although many older adults retain adequate digestive function.
**B. Fat causes pancreatic enlargement.** A larger fat fraction does not imply greater functional parenchymal volume in later life.
**C. Increased sphincter of Oddi pressure.** This is not the characteristic explanation for age-related parenchymal changes.
**D. Lower pancreatic weight.** Late-life atrophy can reduce gland weight despite increasing fat content.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1348, Table 86-7. Saisho et al., Clinical Anatomy 2007, PMID 17879305.

q: בן 87, סובל מסוכרת שנים רבות. מזה שנתיים ללא טיפול תרופתי. ברקע – מחלת אלצהיימר, גר עם מטפל צמוד ומתנייד עם הליכון. המטפל מדווח שהמטופל מרבה לשתות ומטיל שתן בתכיפות גדולה. ירד במשקל 6 ק"ג בחודשים האחרונים. במעבדה המוגלובין A1C – 11%. על פי המאמר ADA Older Adults: Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes-2022 מה הטיפול המומלץ?
o: התחלת טיפול באינסולין ארוך טווח וטיטרציה עד לשיפור בתסמיני ההיפרגליקמיה
מעקב ערכי סוכר 3 פעמים ביום והתאמת טיפול באינסולין קצר טווח לפי טבלה
בגילו ובמצבו אין צורך להקפיד על איזון סוכרת
התחלת טיפול באנלוגים של GLP1 ומעכבי SGLT2
explanation:
Polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss and A1C of 11% indicate symptomatic hyperglycemia. Relieving these symptoms offers immediate benefit even when dementia limits self-management.

**Start a long-acting basal insulin and titrate cautiously to relieve hyperglycemic symptoms.** Engage the caregiver and follow glucose and symptoms to avoid overshooting.

**A. Long-acting insulin.** Once-daily background coverage is relatively simple to administer and adjust.
**B. Short-acting insulin by sliding scale alone.** This requires repeated measurements and dosing decisions and reacts to rather than prevents marked excursions.
**C. Forego glycemic treatment because of age.** Thirst, urinary losses and weight loss already signal harm from the current glucose levels.
**D. Start both GLP-1 and SGLT2 agents.** Additional appetite or weight loss and osmotic diuresis are poor fits for a patient already losing weight and drinking excessively.

Reference · ADA, Older Adults, 2022, recommendation 13.7, Insulin Therapy and Table 13.2 (S197, S201–S202).
